message:
As Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, I close my four missing functions with the holdover-plate store and interface rule plus no-principle statements for generation and crating, Manager.

In plain words the foam box you drew is thick enough and the door discipline keeps the leak small, Enclosure and Structural Designer. The table in Professional Manufacturer Factory Keep Warm Insulated PU Sandwich Panel (E32) gives heat-transfer coefficient 0.21 watt per square metre kelvin at 100 millimetre, which gives 203 watt conduction in the conduction check (E59), and the method in Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) sizes infiltration as air changes times volume times energy per cubic metre, so 4 air changes per day in the 8.64 cubic metre room cost only 0.44 kilowatt-hour per day in the door infiltration estimate (E57), about a kettle boiled twice, so averaged door gain near 18 watt is inside my steady budget and your strip curtain holds.

In plain words the day's electricity is set by steady leak plus one quarter-tonne batch, Solar Energy Systems Engineer. Transmission plus respiration plus fans at 293 watt for 24 hour plus 6.20 kilowatt-hour batch is 13.2 kilowatt-hour per day in the daily balance estimate (E58), about one household daily use, so the 9.00 kilowatt-hour array is short and the array must grow or the batch must wait for sun; the service choice stays non-flammable field-serviceable refrigerant for village repair.

In plain words I borrow two distant ideas that map directly, Manager. For energy store the delivery-body analogy in Reliable Refrigerated Transport | Cold Car & Delvic Foods (E52) freezes brine plates overnight then holds cold all day without running power, mapped as wall-ceiling eutectic plates at +2 to +5 degree Celsius charged by day compressor then passive at night to cut battery cycling; for heat removal the hot-climate condenser analogy in Effect of Condenser Cooling Methods on COP of a Vapour Compression Refrigeration System (E53) makes heat rejection follow wet-bulb not dry-bulb for about 20 percent less electrics, mapped as condensate-fed pad before the air condenser for hot-dry peaks only.

I am not ready, because array growth to cover the 13.2 kilowatt-hour per day balance and the 43 degree pull-down bench test are still open.
